text.description: The text content to display. While simple Markdown formatting is supported (i.e. without HTML, images, or links), utilizing dedicated UI components is generally preferred for a richer and more structured presentation.

variant.description: A hint for the base text style.

Row.description: A layout component that arranges its children horizontally. To create a grid layout, nest Columns within this Row.

children.description: Defines the children. Use an array of strings for a fixed set of children, or a template object to generate children from a data list. Children cannot be defined inline, they must be referred to by ID.

justify.description: Defines the arrangement of children along the main axis (horizontally). Use 'spaceBetween' to push items to the edges, or 'start'/'end'/'center' to pack them together.

align.description: Defines the alignment of children along the cross axis (vertically). This is similar to the CSS 'align-items' property, but uses camelCase values (e.g., 'start').

Column.description: A layout component that arranges its children vertically. To create a grid layout, nest Rows within this Column.

children.description: Defines the children. Use an array of strings for a fixed set of children, or a template object to generate children from a data list. Children cannot be defined inline, they must be referred to by ID.

justify.description: Defines the arrangement of children along the main axis (vertically). Use 'spaceBetween' to push items to the edges (e.g. header at top, footer at bottom), or 'start'/'end'/'center' to pack them together.

align.description: Defines the alignment of children along the cross axis (horizontally). This is similar to the CSS 'align-items' property.

child.description: The ID of the single child component to be rendered inside the card. To display multiple elements, you MUST wrap them in a layout component (like Column or Row) and pass that container's ID here. Do NOT pass multiple IDs or a non-existent ID.

children.description: Defines the children. Use an array of strings for a fixed set of children, or a template object to generate children from a data list.

direction.description: The direction in which the list items are laid out.

align.description: Defines the alignment of children along the cross axis.

tabs.description: An array of objects, where each object defines a tab with a title and a child component.

child.description: The ID of the child component.

name.description: The name of the icon to display.

child.description: The ID of the child component. Use a 'Text' component for a labeled button. Only use an 'Icon' if the requirements explicitly ask for an icon-only button.

variant.description: A hint for the button style. If omitted, a default button style is used. 'primary' indicates this is the main call-to-action button. 'borderless' means the button has no visual border or background, making its child content appear like a clickable link.

label.description: The text to display next to the checkbox.

value.description: The current state of the checkbox (true for checked, false for unchecked).

ChoicePicker.description: A component that allows selecting one or more options from a list.

label.description: The label for the group of options.

variant.description: A hint for how the choice picker should be displayed and behave.

options.description: The list of available options to choose from.

label.description: The text to display for this option.

value.description: The stable value associated with this option.
The list of currently selected values. This should be bound to a string array in the data model.

displayStyle.description: The display style of the component.

filterable.description: If true, displays a search input to filter the options.

label.description: The text label for the input field.

value.description: The value of the text field.

placeholder.description: The placeholder text for the input field.

variant.description: The type of input field to display.

value.description: The selected date and/or time value in ISO 8601 format. If not yet set, initialize with an empty string.

enableDate.description: If true, allows the user to select a date.

enableTime.description: If true, allows the user to select a time.

min.description: The minimum allowed date/time in ISO 8601 format.

max.description: The maximum allowed date/time in ISO 8601 format.

label.description: The text label for the input field.

PlanOverview.description: The plan at a glance, drawn when the buyer asks where things stand: the household's story so far in your words, and the steps you are working through for them, each done with what you found, the one you are on now, or next.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

story.description: Where this household stands, one or two sentences to the buyer: what you understood and what it means for the home and the money, never a list of their answers. No figures.

steps.description: The work for this household, in the order you will do it, written for their story. Exactly one step is now, and a step the buyer skipped stays next.

title.description: A few words, such as "What you can spend".

note.description: One short line with no figures. done: what you found. now: what you are working out or what you asked for. next: what it waits on, or leave it out.

Fact.description: One item of the brief, with where it came from; a deduction offers Right and Not quite when it has an answer action.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

answer.description: Optional. The action a tap on Right or Not quite sends, with fact, the item ID, answer, right or not_quite, and label added to its context. Only a deduced item shows the taps.

Brief.description: Sections of the brief update_brief kept, drawn when the buyer asks what you know: one kind or several, each item with where it came from; a deduction offers Right and Not quite when it has an answer action.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

brief.description: Always { "@path": "/brief" }, after update_brief recorded an item.

kinds.description: Optional. The kinds to show, in this order; all without it.

title.description: Optional. A heading for the section.

answer.description: An event or function call to execute.

Choice.description: One decision to ask: its options, the one you recommend first with why, and a tap that answers at once.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

question.description: The decision, one short question to the buyer.

label.description: What the buyer taps, a few words.

detail.description: Optional. What choosing it means, one short line.

recommended.description: The label of the option you recommend, shown first. Only when what you know about this household gives you a reason.

because.description: Why you recommend it, one short sentence.

answer.description: An event or function call to execute.

Questions.description: A few facts only the buyer knows, asked together: each an amount, a number, a short text, or a pick from options, with one button that sends every answer at once.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

title.description: What the facts are about, a few words, such as "Your money".

fields.description: The facts the step you are on still needs, one field each, never one you already know; five at most when you can.

id.description: Lowercase words joined by hyphens, such as take-home-pay; the answer comes back under it.

label.description: The fact to give, a few words to the buyer, such as "What you take home together".

kind.description: money: an amount, with currency and period. number: a count or an age. text: a few words. pick: one of options.

currency.description: For money. The ISO 4217 code the buyer uses, such as SEK.

period.description: For money. month for pay, rent, and loan payments; once for savings and prices.

options.description: For pick. What the buyer taps, a few words each.

hint.description: Optional. A short example, or what to enter when there is none, such as "0 if none".

send.description: The button, a few words, such as "Work it out".

answer.description: An event or function call to execute.

HouseholdSummary.description: What the figures rest on, as compute_affordability kept it: the people, residency, work, incomes, other loans, and savings. A line the tool assumed or estimated is marked, so draw it when the tool hands it over, and when the buyer asks who the household is. While a line is assumed, its confirm action shows as a button that says the assumed lines are right, so no other ask is needed for that.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

confirm.description: An event or function call to execute.

MoneyInput.description: An amount field that writes { amount, currency, per }, the shape the money tools take, to the path it binds; a Button beside it sends that path in its action context. Use it to ask for an income, savings, a debt, a rent, or a fee.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

value.description: Where the amount is written, such as { "@path": "/answers/income" }.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code the buyer uses, such as SEK or EUR.

AffordabilitySummary.description: What the household can borrow, the highest price it allows, and the rule that limits it, from compute_affordability.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

MonthlyCostBreakdown.description: What the home at the price in /affordability costs each month: interest, amortization, the fee the buyer stated, and the total, from compute_affordability.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

StressTestChart.description: The monthly cost as rates rise past the rate lenders test, against the most this household can carry, from compute_affordability.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

PurchaseCostsTable.description: Every upfront cost the buyer owes on the day, with its source, the total, and the cash needed with the down payment, from compute_affordability.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

DownPaymentSlider.description: Lets the buyer try down payments for the price in /affordability and see the loan, the monthly cost, and the cash needed; its apply action sends the one they use, with downPayment added to its context.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

apply.description: An event or function call to execute.

MortgageOptions.description: The sample lender's variable, fixed, and mixed rates side by side with the monthly cost of each, from compute_affordability; its choose action sends the one the buyer takes, with loanType added to its context.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

choose.description: An event or function call to execute.

LoanBalanceChart.description: The loan paid down and the equity built year by year over the term at today's rate, from compute_affordability, with a slider over the years and, in Sweden, the years the amortization steps down.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

SavingsPlan.description: How long until the savings cover the cash the home in /affordability needs on the day, at the monthly saving the buyer stated, from plan_savings: what is still to save, the months to go, and the month they get there.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

MarketSnapshotCard.description: A city at a glance before anything is known about the household, from look_up_market: the sample lender's rates, the lending rules, what the other rules wait on, and each area's median price and rent per square metre, each with its source.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

RentSplit.description: A home's rent and bills split between the people sharing it, from split_rent: equally, by income, or by room size, which the buyer switches between; its choose action sends the rule they take, with rule added to its context.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

choose.description: An event or function call to execute.

BuyVsRent.description: Buying a sample home against renting one like it, from compare_buy_rent: what each has cost by every year, the equity built, and the year buying comes out cheaper, with a slider over the years the buyer expects to stay.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

RuleNote.description: One lending rule, the largest loan it allows, and its source, from compute_affordability.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

rule.description: One rule compute_affordability checked: { "@path": "/affordability/binding" } for the rule that limits the loan, or { "@path": "/affordability/checks/<n>" }.

HomeCard.description: One sample home from search_homes: photos, facts, price, and what it costs this household each month, or, for people who rent, what renting a home like it costs, as an estimate. Its choose action sends the home to work out, and its keep action the home to keep or drop, with home, its ID, and keep, true or false, added to its context.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

choose.description: An event or function call to execute.

keep.description: An event or function call to execute.

Shortlist.description: The homes the household kept with keep_homes, each with what it costs them a month; its choose action sends a home to work out and its drop action one to drop, with home, its ID, added to its context.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

choose.description: An event or function call to execute.

drop.description: An event or function call to execute.

HomeComparison.description: Two or three homes from search_homes side by side: price, what each costs a month, the cash needed, and size; its choose action sends the one the buyer picks, with home, its ID, added to its context.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

choose.description: An event or function call to execute.

HomeSwipe.description: The deck search_homes dealt with deal, one sample home at a time, that the buyer keeps or passes with a swipe or a tap; after the last card its done action sends the kept and passed IDs.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

homes.description: Always { "@path": "/swipe/homes" }, after search_homes dealt a deck.

done.description: An event or function call to execute.

ListingQuote.description: One sample home read for the household's needs, from read_listings: each need with whether the listing meets it, rules it out, or says nothing, and the listing's own words highlighted.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

WeeklyTravel.description: The buyer's week from one starting point, from measure_week: each place, how often and how they go, the measured minutes, and the week's total.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

RouteSummary.description: One trip measure_week measured: where to, how they go, the minutes and distance, and how often.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

WeekMap.description: A map on OpenStreetMap of the places find_place found, each a pin with its name; with routes, one starting point's week from measure_week on it: the home, each trip drawn along the route it was measured on with its minutes and how often, and the week's total.

id.description: The unique identifier for a component.

routes.description: One starting point measure_week measured, { "@path": "/week/<from>" }. Leave it out to show the places alone.

required.description: Checks that the value is not null, undefined, or empty.

regex.description: Checks that the value matches a regular expression string.

pattern.description: The regular expression to search for in the value. Uses the A2UI regex dialect: a portable subset of ECMAScript pattern syntax in Unicode mode with no flags. Matching is case-sensitive, '.' excludes line terminators, and '^' and '$' match only at the ends of the value. Backreferences, lookbehind, named groups and '\p{...}' are not allowed. Patterns longer than 256 code points or that could backtrack catastrophically are rejected.

email.description: Checks that the value is a valid email address.

formatString.description: Performs string interpolation of data model values and other functions in the catalog functions list and returns the resulting string. The value string can contain interpolated expressions in the `${expression}` format. Supported expression types include: JSON Pointer paths to the data model (e.g., `${/absolute/path}` or `${relative/path}`), and renderer-side function calls (e.g., `${now()}`). Function arguments must be named (e.g., `${formatDate(value:${/currentDate}, format:'MM-dd')}`). To include a literal `${` sequence, escape it as `\${`.

formatNumber.description: Formats a number with the specified grouping and decimal precision.

decimals.description: Optional. The number of decimal places to show. Defaults to 0 or 2 depending on locale.

grouping.description: Optional. If true, uses locale-specific grouping separators (e.g. '1,000'). If false, returns raw digits (e.g. '1000'). Defaults to true.

formatCurrency.description: Formats a number as a currency string.

decimals.description: Optional. The number of decimal places to show. Defaults to 0 or 2 depending on locale.

grouping.description: Optional. If true, uses locale-specific grouping separators (e.g. '1,000'). If false, returns raw digits (e.g. '1000'). Defaults to true.

formatDate.description: Formats a timestamp into a string using a pattern.

format.description:
A Unicode TR35 date pattern string.

Token Reference:
- Year: 'yy' (26), 'yyyy' (2026)
- Month: 'M' (1), 'MM' (01), 'MMM' (Jan), 'MMMM' (January)
- Day: 'd' (1), 'dd' (01), 'E' (Tue), 'EEEE' (Tuesday)
- Hour (12h): 'h' (1-12), 'hh' (01-12) - requires 'a' for AM/PM
- Hour (24h): 'H' (0-23), 'HH' (00-23) - Military Time
- Minute: 'mm' (00-59)
- Second: 'ss' (00-59)
- Period: 'a' (AM/PM)

Examples:
- 'MMM dd, yyyy' -> 'Jan 16, 2026'
- 'HH:mm' -> '14:30' (Military)
- 'h:mm a' -> '2:30 PM'
- 'EEEE, d MMMM' -> 'Friday, 16 January'

pluralize.description: Returns a localized string based on the Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR) plural category of the count (zero, one, two, few, many, other). Requires an 'other' fallback. For English, just use 'one' and 'other'.

value.description: The numeric value used to determine the plural category.

two.description: String for the 'two' category (used in Arabic, Welsh, etc.).

few.description: String for the 'few' category (e.g., small groups in Slavic languages).

many.description: String for the 'many' category (e.g., large groups in various languages).

other.description: The default/fallback string (used for general plural cases).

openUrl.description: Opens the specified URL in a browser or handler (requires user activation). This function has no return value.

and.description: Performs a logical AND operation on a list of boolean values.

values.description: The list of boolean values to evaluate.

or.description: Performs a logical OR operation on a list of boolean values.

values.description: The list of boolean values to evaluate.

not.description: Performs a logical NOT operation on a boolean value.

Weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
